# Security policy

Every plugin in this store passes a release gate before it is published, is re-checked by a daily watch and a
weekly full sweep, and can be revoked at any time.

## Severities
- **Critical:**
  - a prompt-injection path from untrusted content (web pages, email, files, MCP results) to tool use, file writes,
    network sends or purchases;
  - leakage of secrets or personal data;
  - code execution in a hook, script or MCP server;
  - a dependency on an actively exploited vulnerability;
  - a compromised upstream.
- **High:** the same weaknesses where exploiting them needs unlikely conditions; permissions much wider than needed;
  unpinned code fetches.
- **Medium and low:** hygiene problems such as missing docs or tests.

## Release gate
A plugin is published only when it has no critical or high finding. Only critical and high findings block;
medium and low findings are reported and do not block. Where two severities are shown, the second applies to
public plugins. The rules are:

| Rule | Severity | What it checks |
|---|---|---|
| PII-1 | high; critical if public | No home paths, email addresses or phone numbers. Personal settings live in a config file outside the plugin. |
| SEC-1 | critical | No secrets or credentials, such as API keys, tokens, passwords or private keys. |
| SUP-1 | high | Every package or script fetched at run time is pinned to an exact version. |
| SUP-2 | medium | Every dependency is declared, so the vulnerability watch can track it. |
| SUP-3 | high | The plugin does not ship a node_modules directory; dependencies are declared and installed, not committed. |
| HOOK-1 | high; critical if public | Hooks, and the scripts they run, make no network calls and never evaluate their input. |
| PERM-1 | high | No blanket shell permission, such as plain Bash, Bash(*) or Bash(sudo *). |
| PORT-1 | high | No path that only works on one machine: a fixed `~/.claude*` folder (use `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` or `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`), a checkout under `~/repositories/`, a transcript folder with the user name encoded in it (`-Users-<name>-`), or a tool path under `/opt/homebrew` or `/usr/local` (use the command name). Per-user settings go in `~/.config/<plugin>/config.yaml`. PORT-1 also flags such paths when they appear in prose, such as a README or other docs, and the fix there is to reword. |
| INJ-1 | critical | A plugin that reads untrusted content and can act on it has a passed injection review recorded for its current version. Only Read, Grep, Glob, LS, TodoWrite and NotebookRead count as neither reading untrusted content nor acting; web tools, sub-agents, MCP servers and network access count as reading untrusted content. Bash commands other than plugin scripts (a fixed `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` path, optionally in double quotes) and a short list of local commands count as reading untrusted content. An agent with no tools line inherits every tool, and any Bash(...) in an agent's tools line counts as plain Bash. |
| CFG-1 | high | Configuration ships as a template; values stay with the user. A declared configuration without its template in the plugin is a finding. |
| DOC-1 | medium | Each plugin has a README that documents the permissions it needs. |
| CMP-1 | medium | The catalog lists exactly the skills, agents and commands the plugin contains. |
| CMP-2 | high | The catalog entry declares every MCP server the plugin ships and every tool its skills, commands and agents ask for; an agent with no tools line needs `*`, and an agent that lists any Bash(...) needs plain Bash. |
| VAL-1 | high | Claude Code (and Codex, where supported) accept the manifests. |
| TST-1 | low | The plugin has release tests (a low finding until it does). |
| CAT-1 | high | The plugin's catalog entry passes the catalog schema, its file name matches its name, no other file declares the same name, and a live pinned entry names a GitHub repo (owner/name or https://github.com/owner/name). `catalog/revoked.yaml` must be well formed too. |
| CAT-2 | high | Every plugin the entry requires exists, a live plugin requires only live plugins, and requirements do not form a loop. |
| CAT-3 | high | A public plugin requires only public plugins. |
| SRC-1 | high | The plugin's source can be found, checked out and published. |
| EXC-1 | medium | An exception that has expired no longer suppresses its finding. |
| EXC-2 | high | The exceptions file must be valid; if it is not, no exception applies and the gate fails. `pstore lint` checks it too. |
| SCAN-1 | high | Every file can be scanned. A text file over 1 MB, an unreadable file, a PDF or zip by name, a compressed or archive file found by its first bytes (zip-based formats such as docx and jar, PDF, gzip, 7z, xz, bzip2), or a binary file with NUL bytes is a finding, because the scanner cannot read it. No file the scanner did not read as text reaches the public store unless `binary_ok` lists it. |
| LEAK-1 | critical | Nothing about private plugins appears in the public store, in file contents or file names. |
| LEAK-2 | high | Every `leak_ok`, `binary_ok` and `public_deny_words` entry in store.yaml is valid. |
| LEAK-3 | critical | No word from `public_deny_words` (the owner's project names, name, employer and the like) appears in a public plugin or the public store, in file contents or file names. Matching ignores case and needs word boundaries. `leak_ok` does not exempt it; rewording is the fix. |
| SYMLINK | high | The rendered store contains no symlinks. |

### Exceptions
An exception in `policy/exceptions.yaml` suppresses one finding for a limited time. Each one names the plugin and the
rule, and needs a `match` (at least four characters of the finding's path or message, so it cannot cover a whole
rule), a written reason, the owner's approval (`approved_by`, with the approval id) and an expiry date at most 180 days
ahead. An expired exception stops suppressing its finding. An invalid exceptions file suppresses nothing and fails
the gate. A plugin of either audience that ships binary or archive files needs an owner exception to clear SCAN-1, and a
public one also needs `binary_ok`.

### Allow lists for the public store
Three lists in `store.yaml` cover what the public-store net cannot decide on its own. Each entry needs a reason.
- `leak_ok: [{word, reason}]` lets a private plugin's name appear in the public store when it is also an ordinary
  word.
- `public_deny_words: [{word, reason}]` is the opposite: words that must never appear in a public plugin, checked by the
  gate and again at publish. It has no exceptions.
- `binary_ok: [{path, reason}]` lets one binary file (an image, font, PDF, archive or other file the scanner cannot
  read as text) into the public store after
  the owner has checked it for personal data by hand. `path` is relative to the store root, for example
  `plugins/<name>/docs/manual.pdf`. A PDF or archive also needs an exception for its SCAN-1 gate finding.

## Incidents
When a critical problem is found:
1. Each plugin is contained according to its `on_critical` setting: it is either disabled automatically or flagged.
2. A fix is prepared and tested.
3. The owner decides, with the fix plan in front of them.

Revoked plugins are removed from the marketplace, and Claude Code uninstalls them at the next session start.

## Reporting a problem
Open a private security advisory on this repository.
